description.value: The MV Tarahne is a 36-metre historic sternwheeler built in 1917 for passenger and freight service on Atlin Lake, now permanently beached in Atlin and restored by the volunteer-run Atlin Historical Society as a heritage landmark. Launched at a time when Atlin was drawing tourists 'from all over the world,' the vessel embodies over a century of the region's gold-rush, tourism, and Taku River Tlingit history. Cyclists making the remote journey to this far-northern BC community can visit the ship, arrange walking tours with local historians, and even book the vessel for private events.

raw_osm.builder: British Yukon Navigation Company (WP&YR), A. E. Henderson
raw_osm.description: Built 1917 at Atlin for passenger and freight service across Atlin Lake; lengthened in 1928; beached 1958; restored mid-1980s; now hosts public tours, weddings, the annual “Tarahne Tea” event.
raw_osm.name: MV Tarahne
